candidates.name: RegGetValueW
verified_facts: Retrieves a registry value with optional type restrictions
It can ensure returned string values are null-terminated
semantic_limits: A registry value is configuration evidence only and may differ across views, users, or capture times.

candidates.name: RegQueryValueExW
verified_facts: Retrieves registry value type and data
String data may require explicit null-termination checks
semantic_limits: Raw registry readback requires type, length, view, key-handle, and timestamp validation.

candidates.name: RegQueryInfoKeyW
verified_facts: Retrieves registry key metadata and enumeration sizing information
It reports counts and maximum name/data lengths
semantic_limits: Key metadata does not guarantee values remained unchanged during a later enumeration.

candidates.name: RegEnumValueW
verified_facts: Enumerates values of an open registry key
Concurrent mutation during enumeration can invalidate assumptions
semantic_limits: Enumeration output must be joined with key metadata, typed readback, and capture time.

candidates.name: RegEnumKeyExW
verified_facts: Enumerates subkeys of an open registry key
The caller supplies index and buffers sized from key metadata
semantic_limits: Subkey enumeration does not prove configuration relevance or prevent concurrent changes.

candidates.name: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue
verified_facts: Notifies a caller about selected changes to a registry key
Notification lifetime and scope depend on the key handle and flags
semantic_limits: A notification indicates change, not the previous or new value, and cannot prove receipt validity.

candidates.name: Registry Value Types
verified_facts: Defines registry data types such as REG_SZ, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, and REG_DWORD
String values may be stored without proper terminators
semantic_limits: Type definitions do not validate a specific key, value, registry view, or capture.

candidates.name: Registry Functions
verified_facts: Indexes registry query, enumeration, notification, and management functions
Registry APIs return Win32 status codes that require checking
semantic_limits: An API index is not runtime evidence and does not prove any registry read occurred.

candidates.name: GetEnvironmentStringsW
verified_facts: Returns the calling process environment block
The block contains system and user environment variables visible to the process
semantic_limits: The environment block is process-local and does not prove machine-wide configuration or task ownership.

candidates.name: FreeEnvironmentStringsW
verified_facts: Releases a block returned by GetEnvironmentStringsW
The Unicode and ANSI allocation/release pairs must match
semantic_limits: Correct release semantics do not prove the captured environment was complete or authoritative.

candidates.name: GetEnvironmentVariableW
verified_facts: Retrieves one environment variable from the calling process environment
The required buffer size can be returned
semantic_limits: A value can be inherited or overridden and must be correlated with the exact process instance.

candidates.name: ExpandEnvironmentStringsW
verified_facts: Expands environment-variable references using the current process environment
The required destination size is returned
semantic_limits: Expansion output is not canonical path evidence without post-expansion normalization and handle readback.

candidates.name: GetUserProfileDirectoryW
verified_facts: Returns the profile root for the user represented by a token
The token requires query access
semantic_limits: Profile-root resolution does not prove the process is running under that profile or owns the task.

candidates.name: GetProfilesDirectoryW
verified_facts: Returns the root directory containing user profiles
Buffer sizing is explicit
semantic_limits: The profiles root is not the active user's profile and does not establish worktree identity.

candidates.name: GetComputerNameExW
verified_facts: Retrieves a selected form of the local computer name
Computer-name changes may require restart before taking effect
semantic_limits: A matching computer name is not a cryptographic machine identity and can be renamed.

candidates.name: GetCurrentHwProfileW
verified_facts: Returns the current hardware-profile display name and GUID string
The profile GUID can identify hardware-profile-specific configuration
semantic_limits: A hardware-profile GUID does not prove the physical host, disk, or runner process identity.

candidates.name: ProcessIdToSessionId
verified_facts: Maps a process identifier to its Terminal Services session identifier
The process ID must refer to an existing process
semantic_limits: PID-to-session mapping is vulnerable to PID reuse unless joined with process start time and image identity.

candidates.name: WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId
verified_facts: Returns the session identifier attached to the physical console
A sentinel value is returned while no console session is attached
semantic_limits: The active console session is not necessarily the session hosting the canonical runner.

candidates.name: WTSQuerySessionInformationW
verified_facts: Returns selected information for a specified session
Different information classes return different schemas
semantic_limits: Session attributes do not prove process ownership without PID, start-time, token, and image joins.

candidates.name: WTSEnumerateSessionsW
verified_facts: Enumerates sessions on a specified Remote Desktop Session Host server
The returned memory must be released with the documented WTS function
semantic_limits: A session inventory is a point-in-time view and does not identify the canonical runner by itself.

candidates.name: GetConsoleProcessList
verified_facts: Returns process identifiers sharing the caller's console
The count can exceed the supplied buffer capacity
semantic_limits: Console membership is scoped to session and privilege context and is not proof of task ownership.

candidates.name: GetConsoleMode
verified_facts: Retrieves input or output mode flags for a console handle
Mode interpretation depends on whether the handle is input or screen output
semantic_limits: Console mode does not prove stream encoding, redirection target, or receipt byte fidelity.

candidates.name: MultiByteToWideChar
verified_facts: Converts a multibyte string to UTF-16 using a specified code page and flags
Invalid-sequence handling depends on flags and Windows version
semantic_limits: Successful conversion does not prove the original bytes used the claimed encoding.

candidates.name: NormalizeString
verified_facts: Normalizes a Unicode string according to a requested normalization form
The caller can query the required destination length
semantic_limits: Normalization can change binary representation and must not be used to silently rewrite receipt bytes.
